walkthroughs.body_html:
Paper 3: Drama (Open Text) — a core area of GCSE English Literature.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Paper 3: Drama (Open Text) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: What is the dramatic function of a soliloquy?
options: Dystopian fiction predicts what will actually happen in 100 years.
It reveals a character's inner thoughts directly to the audience while the character is alone on stage — a convention granting access to private psychology.
A soliloquy is any long speech a character gives.
A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
When a sentence or phrase runs over from one line of poetry to the next without a punctuated pause, creating flow or surprise across the line break.
Enjambment is when a poem uses no punctuation at all.
Enjambment is when a poem has very long lines.
Dystopian fiction predicts what will actually happen in 100 years.

mcqs.q: What is the function of dystopian fiction?
options: A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
Dystopian fiction predicts what will actually happen in 100 years.
To critique tendencies in the writer's own society by extrapolating them into a nightmarish future — dystopias hold up a warning mirror to the present.
Dystopian fiction is just storytelling set in scary futures.
